info.title: MonitorFlow public API
info.description: Scripts and integrations use `/api/v1` with an API key made under Admin › API keys: `Authorization: Bearer mfk_…`. A key acts as the administrator who made it, within its reach (everything, a customer or a site), its access and its areas. Lists that can grow take `limit` and `cursor` and answer `next_cursor`, null on the last page. Every error has `error`, plain words, and `code`, stable. Writes may carry `Idempotency-Key`; the same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. A key makes up to 600 requests a minute; answers carry `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`, and 429 carries `Retry-After`. See ADR-0101.

get.description:
The last backup, running or finished, when the next automatic one is
due, and the files kept, newest first. `downloads` says whether the
files can be downloaded through the API; when `host_dir` is true they
sit in a host directory only root can read, and are copied from there.
Changes nothing.

post.description:
Asks the updater for a backup of the database and the server's data
directory. Answers at once; the backup shows as `last` in
`GET /api/v1/backups` once the updater takes it, and the oldest file
beyond 7 is removed when it ends. Audited as `server.backup`.

Errors: 409 `conflict` when the deployment has no updater, the updater
is not running, or a backup is already running or asked for. A second
request while one runs is refused, so a retry never takes two.

get.description:
The file itself, `application/gzip`, served as an attachment with
`Cache-Control: no-store`; `Range` requests are honoured. It is a tar
archive of `manifest.json` (format, time, server version, latest
migration), `database.dump` (`pg_dump` custom format of the whole
database: every customer's servers, sites, incidents, commands, users
with their password hashes, API key hashes and the audit log) and
`serverdata/`, the server's data directory: the certificate
authority's private key, the key that signs commands to agents, the
key that opens the stored SMTP passwords, webhook secrets and AI key,
and the mirror signing key. Whoever holds the file can read all of
that and act as the central server towards every agent and relay;
keep it as you would those keys.

Only a global administrator, or a key with access "Administer", reach
"Everything" and the "administration" area, may download one. Each
download is audited as `server.backup.download` with the file name.

Errors: 404 `not_found` for a name the updater did not write or a file
already rotated away; 409 `conflict` when the backups volume is not
mounted in the server or only root can read it on the host.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: A `name` from `files`, like `monitorflow-backup-20261114T030000Z-daily.tar.gz`

post.description:
Makes a new certificate authority. Planned (`emergency` false), the
new one is first only trusted: servers and relays learn to trust it
over their next connections, then it issues once all have moved, then the old one is retired
and its key destroyed, each step taken by the server by itself. In an
emergency the new one issues at once and the old one stops being
trusted 24 hours later: servers and relays that have not connected by
then must be installed again. An emergency request during a planned
change switches it at once. Audited as `ca.rotation.start`; agents and
relays receive the new trust over their next connections, no command
is sent.

Errors: 409 `conflict` when a change is already under way, when more
than one central server instance is running, or when this server has
no certificate authority.

parameters.description: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, a UUID usually. The same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer instead of running twice.

post.summary: Take the next step of the change now
post.description:
Takes the next step without waiting for the servers and relays that
have not moved: makes the new certificate authority the one that
issues, or retires the old one and destroys its key. Those not moved
when the old one is retired must be installed again; `waiting` lists
them first. Audited as `ca.rotation.switch` or `ca.rotation.retire`
with how many had not moved. Not safe to repeat: a second call takes
the step after.

Errors: 409 `conflict` when no change is under way, more than one
central server instance runs, or this server has no certificate
authority.

post.description:
Asks the updater to install `version`: it verifies the release, takes a
backup, replaces the images and checks the new server answers, rolling
back to the previous images if it does not. The central server restarts
meanwhile, so requests may fail for a short while; follow the update with
`GET /api/v1/server-update`, whose `update.id` is the `id` answered here.
Audited as `server.update` with the versions from and to.

Errors: 400 `invalid` when `version` is not a release version or not
newer than the running one; 409 `conflict` when the deployment has no
updater, the updater is not running, or an update is already under
way. A second request while the first runs is refused with 409, so a
retry never installs twice.

Whether the configuration sets `source` or `custom_url`, which the
web interface then cannot change.

An https URL without user, query or fragment; required for `custom`
unless the configuration names one. `null` or empty forgets it.

note.description: When to pick it, in a few words.

models.description: Sorted; empty when the server could not say.

AiSettingsRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /api/settings/ai`: replaces everything but the key, which
is absent, `null` or empty to keep the stored one. The stored key
belongs to the stored provider: another provider forgets it. For an
`openai_compatible` server it also belongs to the stored address: another
address needs the key again, 400 otherwise.

api_key.description:
The provider's API key, stored sealed and never shown again. Absent,
`null` or empty keeps the stored one.

model.description: A model id; for `anthropic`, one of `models`.

AiTestRequest.description:
Body of `POST /api/settings/ai/test` and `/models`, what the form
holds. What it leaves out is taken from the stored settings, the key
and address only for the same provider, and the key of an
`openai_compatible` server only for the stored address.

api_key.description: Absent or empty uses the stored key.

base_url.description: For `openai_compatible`; absent uses the stored address.

error.description: Why it failed, in plain words; `null` when `ok`.

ok.description: The provider answered with this key and model.

AiView.description:
Body of `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/settings/ai`. Readable by every
user, since approvals say when AI is off; holds no key, and the address
only for global administrators.

base_url.description:
The address of an `openai_compatible` server, often inside the
operator's network: null for all but global administrators.

enabled.description: Whether AI diagnoses incidents and proposes commands.

from_config.description:
`[ai] enabled = true` in the configuration, which takes precedence
and locks this page.

has_key.description: Whether an API key is stored, or configured.

models.description: The short list of `anthropic` models, the default first.

command.description: Runs this instead of the proposal, recorded as an `edit`.

AutoUpdateSettings.description: The server-wide settings, as they apply.

enabled.description: The default of sites that inherit it.

enabled_locked.description:
Whether the configuration file sets `enabled`, which the web
interface then cannot change.

failure_threshold.description:
Failed updates, since a rollout started or was resumed, that halt
it; 1 to 1000, 2 by default.

paused.description: Nothing automatic is queued while paused.

AutoUpdateSettingsRequest.description: Body of `PUT /api/settings/auto-update`: the fields to change.

enabled.description:
The default of sites that inherit it; refused while the
configuration sets it. Absent keeps it.

paused.description: Nothing automatic is queued while paused. Absent keeps it.

AvailableRelease.description:
A release newer than the running server, as `GET /api/server-update`
shows it.

first_seen_at.description: When a check first saw it.

BackupKind.description: Why a backup was taken; part of its file name.

error.description: Why it failed, in plain words; `null` unless `failed`.

id.description: The request's ID for one asked for, else the updater's own.

warning.description: What a backup that succeeded left out or noticed.

id.description: The request's ID: the `last.id` of the backup once the updater takes it.

older than backups.

last_success_at.description: When the last one that succeeded finished.

next_at.description: When the next automatic one is due.

downloads.description: The backups volume is mounted: files can be downloaded.

enabled.description: The server shares a volume with the updater, which takes backups.

host_dir.description:

host directory, `BACKUP_DIR`, and are copied from there.

requested.description: "Back up now" waits for the updater to take it.

updater_alive.description: The updater reported within the last two minutes.

CaPeer.description: Where an enrolled peer stands, from its newest certificate.

cut_off.description:
Its certificate comes from a CA the server no longer trusts: it
missed an emergency change and must be installed again.

moved.description: Its certificate comes from the CA that issues now.

name.description: The host name of a server, the name of a relay.

not_after.description: When its certificate expires: it stops counting then.

too_old.description: Its version takes no CA bundle: it must update first.

trusts_all.description: It trusts every CA the server trusts.

CaRotation.description: A change of certificate authority under way.

distrust_at.description: Emergency: when the old CA stops being trusted.

done.description: Those done with the current step.

emergency.description:
Started after a suspected compromise: the old CA is distrusted 24
hours after the switch.

other_fingerprint.description: The new CA while introduced, the old one once switched.

stage.description:
`introduced`: servers and relays learn to trust the new CA, the old
one still issues. `switched`: the new one issues, the old one is
still trusted until it is retired.

total.description: Servers and relays with a valid certificate.

waiting.description: Those not done, by name, up to 50, last seen first.

emergency.description:
`true` after a suspected compromise of the CA's key: the new CA
issues at once and the old one is distrusted 24 hours later.
Default `false`: a planned change, one step at a time.

CaStage.description: The step a change of certificate authority is at.

CaView.description: The certificate authority that issues now, and any change under way.

auto_change_at.description: When a planned change starts by itself if nobody starts one.

cut_off.description:
Servers and relays whose certificate comes from a CA no longer
trusted: they missed an emergency change and must be installed
again. Up to 50.

expires_soon.description: Less than a year left: time to change it.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the CA certificate, lower-case hex.

restored_retired_at.description: Set when a restore brought back a CA this server had retired.

oneOf.description: The change under way; `null` when none is.

CentralRelease.description:
The newest cached release as `central` install commands pin it
(ADR-0054): its version and the SHA-256 of `SHA256SUMS`, of the
installer and of the MSI, as hex. A file is only named when the cache
holds it.

installer_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the installer script, hex; `null` when not cached.

msi_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the Windows installer, hex; `null` when not cached.

path.description:
URL path of its files behind the web interface, without a
trailing slash: `/agent/<version>`.

oneOf.description: `null` when the release could not be fetched or verified.

reachable.description: Whether the source answered; `false` on an offline server.

source.description: Base URL releases are fetched from.

CommandDetail.description:
`GET /api/commands/{id}`: the command and its output, each at most
the last 64 KiB.

health_timeout_s.description:
`self_update`: seconds the new agent has to connect before the
old one comes back; 30 to 3600, 300 by default.

packages.description: Packages to upgrade; empty or absent for all.

ttl_s.description:
Seconds the agent may still start it; [`MIN_TTL_S`] to
[`MAX_TTL_S`], default [`DEFAULT_TTL_S`].

parameters.description: The payload as JSON, for kinds the API knows.

site_count.description: Sites of the customer the user reads, not all of them.

command.description: What will run, or what was rejected.

details.description:

true}` when a silence ended, `{"username", "via"}` when
acknowledged, or `{"step", "steps", "minutes", "told"}` for a
follow-up step.

kind.description:
`opened`, `escalated`, `deescalated`, `resolved`, what a silence
did: `silenced` and `silence_ended` (ADR-0079), `acknowledged`, and
`followed_up` when a follow-up step told someone (ADR-0082).

occurred_at.description: Sample time of the change, or the server clock without a sample.

severity.description: Severity after the change; `null` once resolved.

FollowUpView.description: Where an incident is in its follow-up.

next.description: Who it would tell then, people first; empty when nobody can be.

next_at.description: When the next step is told if nobody acknowledges.

started_at.description: When the first message went out.

state.description:
`waiting` for the next step at `next_at`, `silenced` until a silence
ends then waiting, or `stopped`.

step.description: Steps told so far, and how many there are now.

stop_reason.description:
When stopped: `acknowledged`, `resolved`, `not_critical`, or
`finished` once every step was told.

GroupView.description: A notification that told this incident with others (ADR-0080).

incidents.description:
How many incidents it told that the user may read, this one
included. Members on sites outside the user's scope are not counted.

GuestKind.description: What a Proxmox guest is, which picks its API path.

ImageRef.description:
An image reference by digest: `name@sha256:<64 lower-case hex>`, where
`name` is a registry path like `ghcr.io/kidoly/monitorflow-server` or
`localhost:5000/monitorflow-web`. Tags are refused: a registry can move
them, a digest names the content.

oneOf.description:
Who is told next if nobody acknowledges (ADR-0082); `null` when no
follow-up started: a warning, or not sent yet.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

IncidentView.description:
One incident. Field names and types are part of the API contract: add
fields, never rename or remove them.

acknowledged_by.description:
Who said they are on it, and when (ADR-0082); `null` until someone
does. The name stays when the account is removed.

can_acknowledge.description:
Whether the reader may acknowledge it: open, not acknowledged, and
the reader an operator or above of its site.

hostname.description: The server's hostname, or the relay's name.

instance.description: `""` for a series without an instance.

metric.description: `offline` when the server or relay stopped reporting (ADR-0072).

opened_at.description: Sample times, not the server clock.

peak_value.description: The worst value seen while open.

relay_id.description: Set for a relay's offline incident only (ADR-0072).

severity.description: `warning` or `critical`; the last one while resolved.

silenced.description: Whether a silence ever held back a notification of it.

silenced_until.description:
While open and covered by a silence, when the last one ends
(ADR-0079).

threshold.description: The threshold as it was when the incident opened.

LatestRelease.description: A verified release and what installing it changes.

agent_release_cached.description: The release's agents are already cached for agents.

images.description: The images, pinned by digest, that installing it runs.

newer.description: Newer than the running server: it can be installed.

web_changes.description:
The images differ from the running ones, as the updater reported
them; a local build always differs.

text.description: The license key's text, both blocks.

LicenseTerms.description: What a license key says, once its signature verified.

expires.description: Valid through this whole day, UTC.

server_instances.description: Central servers allowed on the database, the first one included.

LicenseView.description:
Body of `GET /api/license`. Without the Enterprise edition in the build
only `available` is present.

added.description: Central servers added under a license, oldest first.

available.description: Whether this build includes the Enterprise edition at all.

installed_by.description: User name of who installed it.

oneOf.description:
What the installed key says; `null` without a key or when it no
longer verifies.

problem.description: Why an installed key is `invalid`, in plain words.

One command waiting for approval. Field names and types are part of
the API contract: add fields, never rename or remove them.

can_approve.description:
Whether the user may approve this command as proposed, and reject
it. UX hints: the decision routes check again.

command.description: The proposed command, exactly as it would run.

commands_run.description: Commands the incident ran so far, and its limit.

deadline.description:
`opened_at + max_duration_s`: the incident escalates then, and a
decision after it is 409.

diagnosis.description: The AI's text: untrusted, shown as data.

id.description: The pending command; decisions go to `/approvals/{id}/...`.

shell.description:
What runs the command: `posix` (`/bin/sh`) or `powershell`
(Windows PowerShell), from the server's system (ADR-0084).

shell_acceptance.description:
What the server's agent last said it does with these commands:
`accepted`, `off`, `unsupported`, or `null` when unknown (ADR-0076).
Approving is 409 once it refuses them.

snapshots.description:
Whether a change on this server is snapshotted first, on Proxmox
(ADR-0044) or locally (ADR-0094); when not, rollback is limited.

connect otherwise.

names.description: The names the server's certificate is issued for.

ports.

query.description: The PromQL the API ran, filters included.

reason.description: Sent back to the AI with the rejection, and recorded.

oneOf.description: The mirror tools (ADR-0067); not in older releases.

applying.description: A change waits for the updater or is being applied.

default_logs.description: Retention of logs when nothing sets it, like `30d`.

updater_alive.description: A change can be made: the updater runs.

point. Without it, a point is the last sample before it, so a spike
between two points of a long range is not drawn.

Base URL agents reach the package mirror at, written into the
package sources sent to them; a `null` value refuses source
configuration commands.

oneOf.description:
`null` without an updater that reports it, as outside the compose

session_idle_timeout.description: A session unused this long ends, in seconds.

session_lifetime.description: Longest session in the web interface, in seconds.

ServerSettingsRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /api/settings/server`: replaces all three; `null` is the
default.

mirror_public_url.description: An http or https URL without user, query or fragment.

session_idle_timeout.description: Seconds, 300 to 86400, and no longer than the lifetime.

version.description: A release version like `0.2.0`, newer than the running one.

id.description: The `update.id` of the update once the updater takes it.

ServerView.description:
One server. Field names and types are part of the API contract: add
fields, never rename or remove them.

agent_version.description: Version reported by the live stream, else the one last stored.

cert_not_after.description:
Latest expiry among the agent's unrevoked certificates; `null` when
it has none. Past dates mean every certificate has expired.

command_kinds.description:
What its agent last said it does with each command kind: `accepted`,
`off` or `unsupported` (ADR-0076). `null`, or a kind missing here, is

connected_at.description: Start of the current stream, when online.

last_heartbeat.description:
Last message received: from the live stream when online, else the
last time recorded in the database.

offline_alerts.description:
Whether it opens an incident when offline (ADR-0072); muted when
this or `site_offline_alerts` is `false`.

open_incidents.description: Threshold and offline incidents currently open on this server.

package_updates.description: Whether the host can take package updates and sources (ADR-0063).

silenced_until.description: While a silence covers it, when the last one ends (ADR-0079).

via_relay.description: Peer ID of the relay carrying the live stream, if any.

locked.description: The configuration sets it; the page cannot change it.

Shell.description: The shell that runs a server's commands, which decides the rules.

target_id.description: The server, relay, site or customer; absent for `all`.

can_end.description: Whether this user may end it.

agent_auto_update.description:
The site's automatic update override: `null` follows the
server-wide setting (ADR-0055).

agent_auto_update_effective.description: Whether automatic updates apply to the site, override or not.

offline_alerts.description:
Whether servers and relays of the site open incidents when offline
(ADR-0072).

relay_count.description: Enrolled relays of the site, revoked ones included (ADR-0029).

SnapshotSupport.description:
Whether the server can be snapshotted; without it the interface shows
that rollback is limited.

detail.description:
With `cannot_snapshot`: what Proxmox cannot snapshot, like "rootfs
is on storage local (dir), which cannot take snapshots".

oneOf.description: The mapped guest's kind, so the reason can say VM or container.

left_out.description: What a snapshot does not hold, though Proxmox takes one.

method.description:
Which snapshot a change gets when available: `proxmox`, or a local
`lvm` or `zfs` snapshot (ADR-0094).

locked.description: `.env` sets it by hand, which wins over the web interface.

value.description: The value of its `-retentionPeriod` flag, like `90d`.

UpdateRun.description: One update of the server, running or finished.

backup.description: File name of the backup taken first, in the backups volume.

error.description: Why it failed or rolled back, in plain words.

from.description: The version updated from; `null` when the updater did not know it.

migrated.description:
Whether the new server applied migrations: a rollback then needs the
backup restored.

requested_by.description: The user name of who asked.

steps.description: What happened so far, oldest first.

UpdateState.description: Where an update stands; the last three are final.

UpdateStep.description: A step of an update, in plain words.

oneOf.description: A newer release the last check saw.

requested.description: A request waits for the updater to take it.

running_version.description: The version of this server process.

source.description: Base URL releases are fetched from.

oneOf.description: The last update, running or finished.
What the updater last reported; `None` when it never did.

UpdaterView.description: The updater service, as it last reported.

heartbeat_at.description: When it last wrote its status, every 30 seconds while it runs.

oneOf.description: What runs now; `null` before the updater first looked.

link_expires_at.description: Expiry of the user's unused password link, if any.

username.description: The name they sign in with.

tags.name: remediation
tags.description: Commands the AI proposed, waiting for a person

tags.name: metrics
tags.description: Metric queries built by MonitorFlow, never raw PromQL

tags.name: health
tags.description: Probes for load balancers and monitoring: whether the central server's process serves requests and whether its database answers. They need no key and say nothing beyond up or down.

tags.name: server-update
tags.description: Updates of the central server itself, carried out by the updater service of the compose deployment: what runs, whether a newer signed release exists, and the request that installs one. The updater takes a backup first and rolls back by itself when the new version does not start. A global administrator's; with a key, access "Administer", reach "Everything" and the "updates" area.

tags.name: backups
tags.description: Backups of the whole central server, taken by the updater: once a day, before each update and on request; the 7 latest are kept. A backup holds the database of every customer and the server's keys, including the certificate authority's, so only a global administrator lists, takes or downloads them; with a key, access "Administer", reach "Everything" and the "administration" area. Every download is in the audit log.

tags.name: certificate-authority
tags.description: The certificate authority that signs the certificates of the central server, relays and agents for mTLS. These operations show when it expires and change it, planned or after a suspected compromise; they never hand out a key or a certificate. A global administrator's; with a key, access "Administer", reach "Everything" and the "administration" area.

tags.name: settings
tags.description: Settings of the whole central server: where install commands download the agent, the address hosts reach the server at, AI, session lifetimes, the package mirror's address, how long metrics and logs are kept, and automatic agent updates. Values the server's configuration file sets win: they are shown as locked and a request to change them is refused with 409. Every change is in the audit log with the old and new values. Changes are a global administrator's; with a key, access "Administer" and reach "Everything", in the "administration" area, except automatic updates, in the "updates" area.

tags.name: users
tags.description: The accounts of people who sign in to the web interface, and the roles they hold: viewer, operator, approver or administrator, on everything, one customer or one site. Only a global administrator manages them; with a key, access "Administer", reach "Everything" and the "administration" area. A key can grant any role, administrator of everything included, to an existing account, as its maker can. Inviting a user and issuing a password link hand out a credential for a person, so they are left out of the public API and done in the web interface. No change may leave the server without an active administrator of everything, and nobody may disable or remove their own account. Every change is in the audit log.

tags.name: license
tags.description: The Enterprise license key, which allows additional central servers on one database. A single central server needs none. A global administrator's; with a key, access "Administer", reach "Everything" and the "administration" area.
